newsitem.title: SPAIN: BANK OF SPAIN ESTIMATES Q2 GDP GROWTH AT 3.0 PCT.
newsitem.headline: BANK OF SPAIN ESTIMATES Q2 GDP GROWTH AT 3.0 PCT.

text.p: The Bank of Spain estimated gross domestic product (GDP) in the second quarter of 1997 grew by 3.0 percent versus 2.9 percent in the first quarter, according to a report published on Friday.
"According to provisional data, we have estimated that year- on-year real GDP growth was three percent in the period mentioned," the central bank said in its July-August economic report.

The Bank of Spain also estimated domestic demand growth at 2.0 percent year-on-year in the second quarter, versus 1.6 percent in the previous quarter, according to data published by the National Statistics Institute (INE).
Private consumption, which rose 2.8 percent in the first quarter year-on-year, continued to recover, the Bank of Spain added.
However in quarter-on-quarter terms, consumption growth may have slowed.

"With regard to the components of domestic demand, all available indicators confirm that the private consumption recovery has continued, possibly not as strongly as in the previous quarter, in terms of the quarter-on-quarter rate, but exceeding the year-on-year growth rate by perhaps one decimal point (in percentage terms)," the report said.
The central bank said external demand may have contributed one percentage point to GDP growth.
The Bank of Spain said plant investments had continued to expand in the second quarter, while construction investment managed to shake off a negative growth rate.
The central bank attributed the economic improvement to a favourable international trends and the dollar's appreciation, which has contributed to Spain's improved competitivity.
Price stability and fiscal consolidation has also allowed lower interest rates, supporting the economy.
The central bank said labour reforms and growing expectations of Spain's entry into a single currency from the start in 1999 improved household and corporate confidence.
These factors will not only positively affected exports, investment and spending but will also be reflected in housing investment.
